cohort: 1495 women who gave birth at a single tertiary hospital between February 2021 and January 1, 2022
finding: Parity, prior abortions, and smoking were associated with a lower risk of negative birth experience, while immigration, answering questionnaires in person, and cesarean delivery were associated with a higher risk of negative birth experience.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was independently associated with increased negative birth experience risk.
